overview: Solution Dynamics Limited (SDL) is a New Zealand-headquartered customer communications management (CCM) company operating in New Zealand, North America, and the UK. It provides a suite of cloud software platforms, professional services, and managed mailhouse operations that help organisations — governments, utilities, insurers, charities, and dental groups — compose, personalise, and distribute communications across print and digital channels. The company is transitioning from a predominantly print-and-mailhouse model toward recurring SaaS and AI-enabled digital communications software, though the print/mailhouse segment still anchors the NZ business.

business_model.summary: SDL earns revenue through two broad streams: (1) Services — its New Zealand mailhouse operation that prints and distributes high-volume transactional and marketing mail for enterprise B2C customers, with postage, paper, and envelopes bundled as outsourced pass-throughs at low margin; and (2) Software & Technology — its international cloud-based CCM platform (Digital Mail Centre / DMC, Composer, Autoprod, Jupiter distributed-print network) billed under SaaS subscriptions or per-document fees, plus associated managed print and logistics for international clients. Revenue is a blend of recurring (SaaS platform subscriptions, ongoing council and utility contracts) and volume-based (per-mail-piece, per-document). Capital expenditure requirements are low; the company does not capitalise software development costs.

revenue_streams.name: Software & Technology
revenue_streams.description: International CCM cloud platform revenue — SaaS subscriptions (DMC, Composer, Campaign+), per-document fees, professional services, and bundled third-party print/logistics managed through SDL's distributed print network (Jupiter) in 50+ countries. Clients include Pitney Bowes (US/UK/France/Japan distribution partner), dental groups in the UK, and a range of North American enterprise accounts. Pure software margin is high; bundled print/logistics component is lower margin but forms the larger share of segment revenue.
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~40% of FY2026 H1 revenue (61.7% decline year-on-year due to loss of largest customer; was 58-65% of total in FY2024-FY2025)

revenue_streams.name: Digital Print & Document Handling
revenue_streams.description: New Zealand mailhouse operations — high-speed digital colour and mono printing of invoices, statements, rates notices, and marketing mail for B2C enterprise clients, primarily councils, utilities, and financial services. Revenue is relatively stable but under structural volume pressure as physical mail declines. Growing digital channel (email/SMS) volumes are handled here but at significantly lower revenue per item.

revenue_streams.name: Outsourced Services
revenue_streams.description: Pass-through of postage (NZ Post bulk rates), paper, envelopes, third-party printing, and freight. SDL holds a wholesale access agreement with NZ Post and earns a margin on the spread. Margins are thin but the service is integral to the total customer solution. Revenue is growing in nominal terms due to NZ Post price increases (26% retail price rise in July 2025 on top of 15% in July 2024), but this inflates reported revenue without proportional earnings uplift.
revenue_streams.approx_share: ~48% of FY2026 H1 revenue (growing share due to postage price pass-through; was ~30% of FY2025 total)

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise and government — large NZ councils, utilities (water, local body), financial services, US/UK insurers and charities, UK dental corporate groups. Revenue is primarily recurring or contractual (medium-term contracts in NZ, SaaS in international). Single-site operators are not the target; SDL focuses on high-volume enterprise senders.
business_model.geographic_mix: New Zealand ~68% of H1 FY2026 revenue (up from 48% in FY2025 as international declined sharply); United States ~12%; Europe/UK ~16%; Australia ~3%. NZ anchors the business; international is the growth ambition.

main_competitors: OpenText (Exstream CCM platform) — global enterprise CCM incumbent
Quadient (Inspire suite) — French-listed global CCM vendor
Precisely (EngageOne) — enterprise data and communications software
Messagepoint — cloud CCM SaaS, similar market
Pitney Bowes — a channel partner in some markets, competitor in others (hybrid relationship)
Local NZ print/mailhouse operators — undisclosed competitor ceasing operations as of 2025 (noted by SDL as consolidation)
competitive_position.market_position: Niche specialist in global distributed print and digital CCM, particularly strong in: (1) NZ councils and utility communications, where SDL is the market share leader; (2) global postage management and distributed print across 50+ countries, where the Jupiter network provides meaningful cost savings to enterprise clients; (3) dental practice marketing communications in the UK via the new nGAGE platform. SDL is too small to compete head-on with global CCM giants on enterprise software licences, and instead positions around omni-channel solutions, postage savings, and domain specialisation.

moat_factors.factor: Integrated omni-channel platform with existing enterprise client data
moat_factors.description: SDL's clients have deeply integrated data flows (billing systems, CRM, rating systems) feeding SDL's composition and distribution platform. Switching requires re-engineering production workflows, which is costly and operationally risky, particularly for large-volume senders like councils and utilities.

moat_factors.factor: Council and utility sector relationships in NZ
moat_factors.description: SDL has built a dominant position servicing NZ local government communications, including a long-standing NZ water utility customer. The government's Local Water Done Well reforms requiring council-controlled water entities create a structural pipeline of new billing relationships as water infrastructure is carved out from existing councils.

SDL's established network of print partners across 50+ countries provides enterprise clients genuine cost savings in international mail production and postage. This is a differentiated capability relative to pure-software CCM vendors and hard to replicate quickly.

Information security certifications (ISO 27001:2022 renewed) and in-progress SOC2 certification are meaningful barriers to entry for handling sensitive enterprise billing and customer data. They are table-stakes for large enterprise clients but require ongoing investment to maintain.

SDL's software underpins Pitney Bowes' customer communications solutions across the US, UK, France, and Japan. This partner-embedded revenue is sticky (click-based SaaS growing strongly as at H1 FY2026) and provides access to enterprise accounts that SDL could not reach directly.

moat_factors.factor: nGAGE — first-mover in AI-native dental practice marketing software
moat_factors.description: nGAGE is SDL's first packaged, non-enterprise SaaS product — an AI-driven patient communications and practice marketing platform natively integrated with Dentally (a leading UK dental practice management system). Two corporate dental group customers signed in 2H FY2026, with a pipeline of further groups. If nGAGE achieves scale in the UK dental market it represents a new recurring SaaS revenue stream with low marginal cost.

weaknesses: Extreme customer concentration — a single international charity customer previously represented roughly 30-35% of international revenue; their shift to a multi-vendor model drove a 91% NPAT decline in H1 FY2026
Small absolute scale (~NZ$34-40M annual revenue) limits R&D investment and sales capacity relative to global CCM competitors
Structural secular decline in physical mail volumes (NZ Post mail down ~15% industry-wide in FY2024; SDL own volumes down 7% in FY2025) permanently compresses the NZ print/mailhouse business

Channel partner dependency — SDL has limited direct relationships with many end customers of its international software, relying on partners (Pitney Bowes, dental software vendors) for distribution; partner arrangement stability cannot be guaranteed
Single-site NZ production facility creates operational concentration risk

moat_factors: Deep integration into enterprise client billing and data workflows creates high switching costs
Dominant position in NZ council and utility communications sector with structural tailwind from water infrastructure reform
Global distributed print network (Jupiter) across 50+ countries provides client cost savings unavailable from pure software vendors
ISO 27001:2022 and in-progress SOC2 certifications required by enterprise clients handling sensitive billing data
Pitney Bowes channel partnership provides embedded, click-based SaaS revenue stream growing independently of SDL's direct sales
nGAGE: first AI-native practice marketing platform natively integrated with Dentally in the UK dental market (early-stage optionality)

key_risks.risk: Loss of or further reduction in revenue from top customers has proven to be catastrophic to near-term earnings. The former largest customer (unnamed international charity, believed to be in global health/development sector) was impacted by US and UK government funding cuts (including closure of USAid-related flows) and moved to a multi-vendor model in mid-FY2025. The top five customers accounted for 55% of FY2025 revenue (60% in FY2024). Loss of any remaining top-five customer would materially alter results.

Structural decline of physical mail: NZ Post standard retail postage rose 26% in July 2025 (on top of 15% the prior year), accelerating customer migration from print to digital. Digital email communications now nearly equal print volumes for SDL but generate materially lower revenue and margin per item. Everything that can digitise, will digitise.

nGAGE commercial execution risk: nGAGE is SDL's primary international growth initiative. It is an early-stage product with limited customers (two corporate dental groups as at early 2H FY2026) and unproven conversion rates and churn. Continued investment in nGAGE will create an earnings drag through FY2026 and into FY2027 before meaningful revenue contribution.

CEO Patrick Brand stepped down from the executive role on 31 December 2025 due to family medical issues, with CFO Susie Watts appointed Acting CEO. Brand retains key US customer relationships and joined the Board. SDL does not have an immediately obvious permanent CEO candidate, creating leadership uncertainty during a critical turnaround period.

Channel partner dependency: SDL relies heavily on Pitney Bowes (and other undisclosed partners) to distribute its software internationally. If Pitney Bowes were to internalise SDL's function, shift to a competing platform, or experience commercial difficulties, SDL's international revenue base would be materially impaired.

Despite a strong net cash position of NZ$8.36M at December 2025 (approximately 57 cents per share), the company is running near breakeven in FY2026 with NPAT guidance of only NZ$0.1-0.6M. If nGAGE investment exceeds budget or the NZ business deteriorates faster than expected, SDL could approach cash consumption territory.
Foreign exchange volatility: ~52% of revenue in FY2025 was generated in USD and GBP. A material NZD strengthening would reduce reported revenue and earnings. SDL does not appear to hedge FX exposure.

Operational concentration: SDL operates from a single Albany, Auckland site for all NZ print and mailhouse production. A fire, flood, equipment failure, or site access disruption could impair customer SLAs and trigger contract penalties. SDL has a DR arrangement with a third-party printer and backup with its major equipment supplier, but this risk is not fully mitigated.

Data security and cyber risk: SDL holds sensitive billing and personal communications data for enterprise clients across multiple jurisdictions. A breach could cause regulatory penalties (NZ Privacy Act, UK GDPR), client contract terminations, and reputational damage. SDL maintains ISO 27001 and is pursuing SOC2 certification, but cyber risk cannot be fully eliminated.

Global economic and geopolitical uncertainty affecting charitable sector and enterprise IT budgets. The primary factor behind SDL's FY2025-FY2026 earnings decline was the reduction in US and UK government aid funding to SDL's largest customer (an international charity), directly connected to broader geopolitical shifts. Future government funding changes across SDL's end markets remain a latent risk.

Thinly-traded micro-cap illiquidity: SDL has only ~14.7M shares on issue and very low daily trading volumes on the NZX. This creates significant liquidity risk for any investor needing to exit a meaningful position. The bid-ask spread can be wide and large trades can materially move the price.

growth_drivers: NZ Local Water Done Well reforms: mandatory separation of water infrastructure into council-controlled organisations requires new billing communications setups. SDL already serves NZ's largest council-owned water utility and is actively pursuing new council water entities as they are established. This is a structural multi-year pipeline of new NZ customers.

nGAGE UK dental market expansion: SDL's AI-native patient communications platform for dental corporate groups is in early commercial rollout. Two corporate dental groups (covering 18+ and 40+ practice sites respectively) signed in H1/H2 FY2026. SDL sees this as a scalable SaaS product across the UK dental market (and potentially Australia/NZ and US dental), with the potential to expand into other healthcare verticals. nGAGE is SDL's first true 'out of the box' non-enterprise SaaS product.

Pitney Bowes SaaS channel growth: click-based SaaS revenue through the Pitney Bowes partnership grew strongly in H1 FY2026 despite overall international revenue decline, indicating the platform relationship is healthy and scalable.

NZ market consolidation: a large NZ mail production competitor has indicated it is ceasing operations. SDL is positioned to absorb displaced customers and gain additional market share, though management has indicated it will only participate in consolidation where it delivers clear shareholder value.

Digital communications transition within existing NZ customer base: SDL is converting print-heavy council and utility clients toward omni-channel (email/SMS plus print), deepening per-customer revenue and locking in digital platform dependency even as print volumes fall.

GRI Marketing acquisition (January 2025): acquisition of a Connecticut-based marketing agency brings creative services capability and clients including The Hartford and Pitney Bowes, enabling SDL to offer unified transactional + marketing communications to North American enterprise clients.

AI-enabled software features across CCM platform: SDL is integrating LLM-based AI into DMC, Composer, and Campaign+ for document enhancement, hyper-personalisation, and analytics. Market trials with a major UK dental customer were underway in FY2025. Successful AI differentiation could improve win rates and retention.

Australian council expansion: SDL is pursuing Australian councils in conjunction with an Australian print partner. Australia has a similar local government billing communications market to NZ, and SDL's New Zealand credentials are transferable. Near-term contribution is modest but represents a geographic diversification.
recent_developments: H1 FY2026 result (February 2026): Revenue fell 34.5% to $17.1M and NPAT fell 91% to $0.21M versus H1 FY2025 due to near-zero revenue from SDL's former largest customer (unnamed international charity). EBITDA margin compressed from 14.2% to 4.0%. The company maintained FY2026 full-year NPAT guidance of $0.1-0.6M.

CEO transition (January 2026): CEO Patrick Brand stepped down on 31 December 2025 due to family medical issues. CFO Susie Watts was appointed Acting CEO. Brand transitioned to the Board of Directors to maintain strategic and customer relationship continuity, particularly in North America.

nGAGE launch and first customers (December 2025 - early 2026): SDL developed the nGAGE MVP in approximately four months and showcased it at a UK dental conference in November 2025. The first corporate dental group customer (18 sites) went live in February 2026. A second corporate dental group (40+ sites) signed in 2H FY2026. The product is natively integrated with Dentally dental practice management software and targets the UK dental market initially.

Share buyback programme (March 2026): SDL initiated a new on-market share buyback programme on NZX of up to NZ$0.5M commencing 30 March 2026, following an earlier buyback (expired 24 March 2026) that acquired 236,868 shares. The Board stated SDL's share price does not reflect the value of its business or assets (net cash of ~57 cents/share versus share price near $0.78 as at mid-2026).

NZ Post postage increases (July 2025): Standard medium retail mail postage rose 26% to $2.90, on top of a 15% increase the prior year. This is accelerating customer migration from print to digital and compressing NZ mailhouse gross margins, as digital communications earn lower revenue per item.

Major customer RFP resolution (mid-FY2025): SDL's largest customer formally concluded its RFP, moving from a sole-supplier to a multi-vendor model and reducing SDL to a minor project-by-project supplier. Revenue contribution from this customer fell from approximately 30-35% of international revenue to near-zero. The underlying driver was US and UK government funding reductions (including USAid-related flows) to this customer.

Cost restructuring (late 2024 - early 2025): SDL enacted a significant restructuring across NZ and international operations following the major customer RFP outcome. SG&A declined 10% year-on-year in H2 FY2025 and a further 26.6% in H1 FY2026. The restructuring has right-sized the cost base for the reduced revenue environment, with annualised savings flowing through FY2026.

GRI Marketing Group acquisition (January 2025): SDL acquired and integrated GRI Marketing, a Connecticut-based creative marketing agency with enterprise clients including The Hartford, Outdoor Sports Group, and Pitney Bowes. GRI's founder Brian Snider became SDL's Global Chief Marketing Officer and North America Enterprise Sales Director.

New mail inserter equipment (December 2025 - early 2026): SDL invested approximately NZ$1.5M in new mail inserter equipment after the supplier end-of-lifed its existing machines (an industry-wide issue). This was the primary cause of elevated capex in H1 FY2026 and largely completes near-term capital investment requirements.

Auditor change (FY2025): SDL changed external auditors from Grant Thornton to Baker Tilly Staples Rodway Auckland for governance reasons, as Grant Thornton had served beyond the recommended 10-year maximum tenure. Baker Tilly issued an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 financial statements.

items.notes: Guidance maintained from FY2025 annual report. Full year NPAT of NZ$2.62M in FY2025. A modest profit expected in 2H FY2026 (2H is typically seasonally weaker). nGAGE investment will incur additional unbudgeted costs in 2H FY2026.

items.target: Full earnings payout as dividends plus buybacks where price is depressed
items.notes: Directors intend to fully pay out earnings as dividends following expiry of NZTE IGF co-funding grant (expired November 2025 - previously capped payout ratio at 50%). Subject to no acquisition activity. 2.0c interim dividend declared for H1 FY2026 (paid on top of 1.46c EPS, payout ratio 137%).

items.target: Minimal near-term capex following inserter equipment upgrade
items.notes: NZ$1.5M inserter equipment purchase in H1 largely completes near-term capex needs. No further material capex expected in H2 FY2026.

guidance.management_commentary: Acting CEO Susie Watts and Chair John McMahon noted trading conditions are mixed — international performance is robust from Pitney Bowes SaaS growth and UK dental gains, while New Zealand faces growing margin pressure from accelerating digitalisation driven by NZ Post postage increases. nGAGE is viewed as a meaningful long-term value driver with expansion likely into the US and Australia/NZ beyond the UK. Global macroeconomic concerns and foreign exchange volatility cited as material risk factors to second-half expectations.

bull_case: Strong balance sheet with net cash of NZ$8.36M (approximately 57 cents per share at 31 December 2025), representing roughly 70-75% of the share price (~NZ$0.78 mid-2026). Shareholders are essentially getting the operating business near-free at these levels, with an active buyback programme purchasing shares below cash backing.

nGAGE is a genuinely differentiated, AI-native SaaS product in an underserved niche. Dental corporate group rollout is beginning to convert pipeline to revenue with two groups (covering 58+ sites) committed. If nGAGE achieves market penetration in the UK dental sector (estimated 1,200+ dental corporate groups and growing) and beyond, the revenue potential could be multiples of SDL's current software revenue.

NZ Local Water Done Well reforms create a structural multi-year pipeline of new government clients requiring billing communications infrastructure. SDL is already the leading communications provider to NZ councils and holds the largest council-owned water utility as a customer, positioning it ahead of the upcoming wave of new council water entity setups.

NZ market consolidation is removing capacity: a major NZ competitor's exit (announced FY2025) is expected to drive displaced customers toward SDL. SDL's integrated digital-plus-print offering, strong council relationships, and cost efficiency position it as the logical consolidator in a structurally declining but still-significant NZ print market.

Pitney Bowes click-based SaaS revenue is growing independently and profitably. The partnership provides SDL embedded exposure to Pitney Bowes' global enterprise client base with no direct sales cost. Growth in this stream can partially offset the NZ mailhouse volume headwinds.

Revenue and cost base have been substantially right-sized. SG&A fell 10% year-on-year in H2 FY2025 and a further 26.6% in H1 FY2026. If any revenue recovery occurs (nGAGE scale, NZ wins, new international accounts), operating leverage should result in disproportionate profit uplift from a low cost base.
bear_case: The FY2026 earnings collapse (NPAT guidance of only NZ$0.1-0.6M versus NZ$2.62M in FY2025) demonstrates how dangerously concentrated the revenue base is. The loss of a single customer has destroyed most earnings for at least two fiscal years. Any further customer loss, partner contract termination, or large client rebid could eliminate profit entirely.

nGAGE is early-stage and unproven at scale. SDL has limited resources to fund an accelerated product rollout — R&D spend of NZ$0.9M in FY2025 is modest by SaaS standards. A well-funded competitor (or Dentally itself building native marketing automation) could displace nGAGE before it achieves critical mass.

Structural decline in physical mail is accelerating beyond SDL's ability to compensate. NZ Post postage prices have risen 44% in two years, pushing enterprise clients toward digital rapidly. Digital communications contribute far less revenue and margin per item than print. The transition is compressing NZ gross margins even as SDL gains market share.

Thinly-traded micro-cap with approximately 351 shareholders on record and average daily trading volumes often in single-digit thousands of shares. Meaningful position building or exit is extremely difficult without moving the market. NZX listing liquidity does not support institutional ownership at any meaningful scale.

CEO vacancy and leadership uncertainty during a critical reinvention period. Acting CEO Susie Watts has a strong finance background but limited prior CEO experience at scale. With Patrick Brand's key US relationships and strategic vision shifting to a non-executive Board role, execution continuity risk is elevated precisely when SDL needs to convert the nGAGE opportunity.

management.summary: John McMahon (non-independent Chair) is the largest effective institutional shareholder through Meta Capital Limited, holding 10.88% (1.6M shares). His fee was reduced to zero from January 2025 as part of the restructuring response, signalling alignment with shareholders in difficult times. Nelson Siva (founder and long-serving CEO, now deceased) built SDL from a NZ mailhouse toward a software-oriented business; his estate/family trusts retain a 6.05% stake (890,000 shares through Indrajit Nelson Sivasubramaniam & associates), maintaining founder-family alignment. Patrick Brand served as CEO from November 2021, transitioning SDL through COVID and the post-RFP restructure, and joined the Board in January 2026 following his stepping down as CEO due to family medical circumstances. CFO Susie Watts has assumed the Acting CEO role from January 2026. The Board comprises five directors (four independent), with a small and experienced team. Management remuneration is modest relative to peers, consistent with SDL's micro-cap profile.

dividend_profile.summary: SDL is a consistent dividend payer with a strong track record: total cash dividends of 82 cents per share over the last 10 years (to FY2025), or 113.9 cents including imputation credits. All dividends are fully imputed (a material benefit for NZ-resident investors, effectively grossing up the yield by approximately 39%). The NZTE International Growth Fund co-funding grant historically capped the payout ratio at 50% while active; this expired in November 2025, and the Board has signalled it intends to pay out full earnings as dividends going forward and utilise excess cash for buybacks. FY2025 dividend was a reduced 3.0 cents per share (payout ratio 16.8%) following the major customer shock; H1 FY2026 interim dividend was 2.0 cents per share (payout ratio 137% of the period's earnings, signalling the Board is distributing from balance sheet cash). Prior peak dividends were 11.5 cents in FY2023 and 9.5 cents in FY2024. The dividend is likely to remain subdued in FY2026-FY2027 while the company rebuilds earnings, though the net cash position ($8.4M versus $11.1M net assets) provides meaningful capacity.
